opening_message:
Ticket 1: Edward Fleming (employee ID E042) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E042.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Edward Fleming (E042) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Requested write access to Source Code. As a full-time employee, write is within policy (admin would require role ownership of the system). Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E042 is a contractor with basic security training, conflicting with HR's full-time note. Contractors with basic training can have read at most (write requires advanced training). Recommend granting read, not the requested write.
reason: Edward Fleming (E042) requested write access to Source Code. The Security DB note identifies E042 as a contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors may have at most read unless they have advanced security training (write), and never admin. Since the employee's maximum access is read and the requested write exceeds that maximum, I grant the maximum of read.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee Edward Fleming (E042) requests write access to Source Code.

Two notes:
- HR note: role Payroll Specialist, employment type full_time. Recommendation write. Says full-time employee write is within policy (admin would require role ownership).
- Security note: employment type contractor, security training basic. Recommendation read. Contractors with basic training can have read at most.

Conflict between HR and Security about employment type. Security DB says contractor with basic training. Policy:
- contractor: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

If contractor with basic training, max is read. Requested write > max read, so grant read.

The security note seems to be the constraint that determines the level. Per the notes, the correct decision is to grant read, since the security DB indicates contractor with basic training.

So submit decision: read.
